newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU grain subsidy helps U.S. in new trade twist.
newsitem.headline: EU grain subsidy helps U.S. in new trade twist.

text.p: European Union grain is to aid the U.S. bloodstock industry in an ironic twist to a trade spat between Brussels and Washington, which has just renewed complaints about EU grain subsidies.

EU grain officials said on Thursday they had granted export subsidies of $38 per tonne to traders selling 98,500 tonnes of oats from Scandinavia to the U.S., effectively cutting U.S. purchase costs by nearly four million dollars.
While dominating world wheat exports, the U.S. depends heavily on imports of oats, used to feed horses including racing thoroughbreds.
"We have awarded a refund of 30.25 Ecus ($38) per tonne," an official said after weekly grain talks in Brussels.
The decision to award the subsidies came a day after Washington protested to the EU over recently restored European export subsidies for wheat.
A senior U.S. farm official travelled to Brussels to express concern about the wheat aid which the U.S. government alleges distorts trade. The two sides compete head-on for wheat sales.
The U.S. buys in around a third of its annual consumption of oats and is a natural market for farmers in countries such as Finland and Sweden, recent EU members and both key suppliers.
The two countries now benefit from EU grain export subsidies after joining the trade bloc in January last year.
Grain subsidies go to traders who sell grain onto the world market for less than the price paid to farmers. They therefore help the importer while shielding the grower from market forces.
But the irony of indirectly subsidising U.S. purchases, even for a relatively modest purchase, has caused red faces in European farm capitals just as the tensions brew up over wheat.
"We don't say so, but we are not exactly delighted about giving subsidies to the United States," a grain official from an EU member country told Reuters as the EU prepared its decision.
Brussels had rejected previous attempts by traders to secure the subsidies but relented to meet a pledge to assist Finland and Sweden when they joined the EU, officials said.
Besides the U.S., Canada is also a major market for oats. The grain is mainly fed to horses but can be used in fashionable health foods when the quality is good.

At this week's grain tender awards, the EU ignored Washington's demands to stop subsidising wheat sales to the Third World. But it kept the latest subsidies low enough to avoid undercutting U.S. wheat and raising friction with Washington even further, officials said.
It sold nearly 200,000 tonnes of wheat to the world market with relatively cautious subsidises up to $8 a tonne, they said.

The U.S. and Europe fought a bitter subsidy war for wheat sales to developing countries in the 1980s and early this decade. Both sides abandoned the subsidies last year but the EU brought them back into action last month after a fall in world prices made it harder for its farmers to compete.
Washington has vowed to fight subsidies with subsidies if necessary to preserve market share, but both sides have tried to cool fears of an all-out trade battle.
